Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the fourth innings! The South African players have made their way out to the middle. Shadman Islam and Mahmudul Hasan Joy are at the crease. Keshav Maharaj will start with the ball.
... Fourth innings ...

South Africa have set a target of 274 runs for Bangladesh. The hosts came into bat with a lead of 69 runs, although they did not get enough time at the crease due to early stumps on Day 3. The hosts started positively in the morning session on Day 4 by losing only a single wicket of Sarel Erwee. Their worse nightmare was yet to come, as Bangladesh roared back in the afternoon session. The visitors took 4 wickets in that session and did manage to put a lid over the run rate as well. Later, only Ryan Rickelton was the stand out batter for South Africa, who did manage to bat till the end but could not apply the same pressure with the tail-enders. South Africa lost their last three wickets in 8 deliveries and that would hurt them a lot. Bangladesh bowlers turned on the heat with the ball since the afternoon session. It was a combination of pace and spin attack that did the trick for them. Mehidy Hasan was the pick of the bowlers with three wickets. Ebadot Hossain also enjoyed his time out with the ball, as he grabbed three wicket as well. The onus is now on the Bangladeshi batters. They have about an hour and a whole day's play in hand to chase the target. Will they be able to convert it into a win? Do join us in a short while for the chase.

OUT! LBW! That is it! Ebadot Hossain gets the last wicket. This was a length ball, jagging back in from outside off. Duanne Olivier looks to block it off the back foot but he misses as the ball sneaks through his bat. Olivier gets hit on his pad and Bangladesh appeal. The umpire agrees but Olivier sends it upstairs. The Ball Tracker rolls in and it indicates three reds. South Africa are bowled out for 204!
Review! Duanne Olivier opts for a review for an lbw decision going against him. The UltraEdge shows no bat is involved. The Ball Tracking shows three reds and the on-field decision stays.
Full length, angled into the pads. Duanne Olivier tucks it to short mid-wicket.
BEATEN! Full length, outside off. Duanne Olivier tries to push it away. He gets beaten on the outside edge.
Full length, outside off. Duanne Olivier lets it be.
OUT! LBW!
Duanne Olivier is the last man in.

OUT! RUN OUT! Oh, dear! South Africa are losing their way here! Cricketing suicide from South Africa! Lizaad Williams looks to steal a run off the misfield but ends up throwing away his wicket. This was a short ball, around middle. Ryan Rickelton pulls it towards square leg for a run. The fielder there hurls a wayward throw towards the keeper. Liton Das fails to grab the ball and Williams looks to take another run. Ryan isn't interested and he sends him back. Shadman Islam at point, throws the ball back to the keeper who whips the bails off. Williams is well short of his crease.
Is that a run out? The umpire takes it upstairs to confirm. The replays confirm Lizaad Williams is way short of the crease when the bails were coming off.
Tossed up, around off. Ryan Rickelton taps it to the off side and takes a single.

DRINKS! Bangladesh needed a moment of inspiration and that came in from the fielder. They have broken the eighth-wicket stand now. Bangladesh are right back in the game. They need just two more wickets to end this South African innings. How much can the tail-enders add to the scoreboard? Will they be able to reach the 300-run mark? Stick around to find out. Lizaad Williams is the new batter in for South Africa.

Is that a run out? A direct hit at the bowler's end and Simon Harmer might be in trouble. Yes, the replays roll in and it shows that Harmer is well short of his crease. This was a flatter ball, outside off. Harmer cuts it through the cover region. He completes the second run with ease and looks to steal the third run. Although, Nurul Hasan (sub) collects the ball from the deep and scores a direct hit at the non-striker's end. South Africa lose their eighth wicket now!
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Ryan Rickelton rocks back and pushes it through the off side for one run. 200 comes up for South Africa!
Fuller, on leg. Simon Harmer tucks it to square leg for a quick single.
SIX! BANG! Good use of the feet from Harmer! Tossed up, pn off. Simon Harmer skips down the track and bludgeons it over the deep mid-wicket region for a biggie.
Floated, on a length, on leg. Simon Harmer wrists it to short leg.

Back of a length, just outside off. Ryan Rickelton dabs it onto the deck.
A full ball, on middle. Ryan Rickelton flicks it to the mid-wicket fielder.
A short ball, angling down leg. Ryan Rickelton sways away from the line of the ball.
Fuller in length, outside off. Ryan Rickelton squeezes it out.
Good-length delivery, around off. Ryan Rickelton keeps it out.
Flatter and quicker, on off. Simon Harmer pushes it back to the bowler.
Floated, on a length, around middle. Simon Harmer sits back and tucks it to square leg.
A loopy ball, outside off. Simon Harmer reverse-sweeps but the ball hits the first slip fielder.
Flatter and on off. Ryan Rickelton rocks back and pushes it to cover for a run.
Floated, full and outside off. Ryan Rickelton looks for a reverse-sweep but he misses.
A full ball, on middle. Simon Harmer eases it to long on for a run.
Length ball, on the pads. Simon Harmer nudges it to mid-wicket for one. The lead moves to 259.

On a length, around off. Simon Harmer looks to push it away. The ball goes towards the slip cordon off the outside edge. Mahmudul Hasan Joy, at second slip, dives to his left and makes a sharp stop. Saves a certain boundary to be honest.

BEAUTY! Ebadot Hossain asking the right questions. A length ball, outside off. This one holds its line after hitting the deck. Simon Harmer tries to defend it inside the line but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Full length, outside off. Simon Harmer drives it to cover but straight to the fielder.
A length ball, on middle and leg. Ryan Rickelton stays back, clips it to square leg for one.
Length ball, on the pads. Ryan Rickelton tucks it to mid-wicket.

Full, on off. Simon Harmer blocks it on the front foot.
Floated, full and down leg. Simon Harmer tucks it to the leg side.

Tosses it up, on off stump. Ryan Rickelton goes back and defends it to the off side.

Full length, outside off. Ryan Rickelton pushes it to cover.

Taskin Ahmed goes for another yorker, even this is in the blockhole. Simon Harmer digs it out watchfully. Taskin Ahmed is bowling with fire with an injured shoulder. This is excellent stuff.

OUT! LBW! What a delivery! Taskin Ahmed gets his second wicket here. Keshav Maharaj walks back on a timid score. A full-length ball, slanting in from outside off. Keshav Maharaj tries to defend it out on the front foot but misses to get any blade on it. He gets pinged on his pad. Taskin Ahmed appeals and the umpire raises his finger in a flash.
Fuller, on off. Keshav Maharaj drives it to extra cover. The fielder there dives to his right to make a sharp stop.

FOUR! Ryan Rickelton choosing the aggressive path now. Full length, outside off. Ryan Rickelton leans in and drives it through covers for a boundary. This is as good as it gets for Ryan Rickelton. He seems to have his eye in at the moment.
Uppish but safe! Tossed up, just outside off. Keshav Maharaj skips down the track and just chips it over the mid off fielder for a brace.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Ryan Rickelton cuts it past the cover-point fielder for one run.
FOUR! A wayward ball, full and down leg. Ryan Rickelton kneels and sweeps it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.

Nicely done! Another ball, full and outside off. Maharaj gets forward and drives it through the vacant cover region. The batters take three runs. The cover fielder gives it a chase and does well to keep the ball in play.
Full and outside off. Keshav Maharaj drives but finds the wide mid off fielder.
Keshav Maharaj is the new batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Mehidy Hasan strikes yet again! Lovely delivery from the youngster! Hasan tosses it up nicely, outside off, from 'round the wicket, enticing the batter to drive. Mulder prods and looks to drive it through cover. Although, he only manages a thick outside edge which goes straight to Yasir Ali at first slip who takes a sharp catch. South Africa lose their sixth wicket now!
Commentary.Howout: c Yasir Ali b Mehidy Hasan

NOT OUT! That was clearly a bump ball! A very full ball, outside off, almost a yorker-length delivery. Mulder looks to dig it out but he misses and the ball sneaks under his bat. Bangladesh appeal for a caught behind but the on-field umpires are not sure. They take it upstairs. The replays roll in and it shows that the ball bounced off the surface before going to the keeper.

Is it out? The umpires converge and decide to take it upstairs. The soft signal is not out. The replays show that the ball bounced just beofre the blade. The UltraEdge confirms that it is a bump ball. The final decision is NOT OUT. Wiaan Mulder survives.

A length ball, around off. Ryan Rickelton keeps it out.

We are back for the final session of Day 4! The players have made their way out to the middle. Wiaan Mulder and Ryan Rickelton to resume their innings. Taskin Ahmed will start with the ball.
... Day 4, Session 3 ...

This afternoon session has truly belonged to one team and that is the visiting side. While one end worked with pace, the other one was single-handedly managed by Mehidy Hasan. The bowlers worked in tandem, with the fielders being much more attentive on the field. This certainly changed the scenario for Bangladesh. South Africa only managed to score 52 runs in 28 overs. The Bangladeshi bowlers picked up four wickets in this session, out of which two belonged to Hasan, while Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain picked a wicket each. The South African batters were not able to score as freely as they did in the morning session and that might hurt them a lot. It could’ve gotten worse for the home side but with some rub of green they managed to not lose any more wickets till Tea. South Africa lead by 226 runs now. They would look to get near the 300-run mark before speculating any declaration for their side. In whose favor will the game shift towards in the final session of Day 4? To find out, join us at 1900 IST (1330 GMT).

OH DEAR! Khaled Ahmed drops an easy chance and he is down on the deck. A length ball, around off. Wiaan Mulder tries to flick it away. The ball lobs to the left of the bowler off the leading edge. Khaled Ahmed moves to that side but is unable to grab it cleanly.

DROPPED! Wiaan Mulder does not depart on a golden duck in this innings. Touch short, outside off. Wiaan Mulder tries to cut it away. The ball takes the outside edge and goes towards the man at first slip. He fails to grab the ball and it goes past him. The batters take a single.
Wiaan Mulder walks out to bat. He is on a King pair.

OUT! CAUGHT! Mehidy Hasan strikes again in the afternoon session. Exceptional effort in the field by Shadman Islam. It is floated, full and on off. Kyle Verreynne tries to reverse-sweep it. He does not middle it though. The ball takes the under-edge, lands on his boot and lobs to the left of silly point. Shadman Islam shows good presence of mind here, as he was up in the air trying to evade the reverse-hit. He later realises that the ball is in the air to his left. He then stretches out his left and takes a stunning catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Shadman Islam b Mehidy Hasan

It is a loopy ball, around off. Kyle Verreynne gets low and tries to sweep it away but misses. The ball sneaks under his blade and hits him on the pads. Mehidy Hasan appeals and the umpire raises his dreaded finger. Kyle Verreynne takes the review straightaway. The UltraEdge shows no bat is involved. The Ball Tracking shows that the ball is missing the wickets. The umpire is forced to overturn his original decision. Kyle Verreynne survives. This is the eighth decision that has been overturned in this Test match so far.

Hossain bowls it full, around off. Ryan defends it off the front foot.

Flatter and around off. Ryan Rickelton rocks back and punches it to cover.
A full ball, around off. Kyle digs it out to the off side for a single.

DRINKS! South Africa lead by 201 runs at the moment. But Bangladesh has made inroads in this game with some crucial wickets. With two new batters at the crease, Bangladesh will be hoping to end things early and come back out to chase before Stumps. How will the fifth-wicket stand fare for the Proteas? Stick around to find out.

OUT! CAUGHT! OH MY GOD! Yasir Ali, you beauty! In the morning session, Ali did drop a catch at slips. But this chance is even tougher and he grabs it with a single hand. Temba Bavuma cannot do anything about it other than walking back to the dressing room. Coming to the delivery - it is a length ball, around off, shaping away off the deck. Temba Bavuma hangs his blade away from his body. The ball takes the outside edge, goes to the left of first slip. Yasir Ali dives to that side and takes a stunning one-handed catch. Bangladesh are back in the game now.
Commentary.Howout: c Yasir Ali b Ebadot Hossain

Edged but safe! Flatter and quicker, going on with the angle from just outside off. Temba Bavuma sits back to block but it goes off the thick outside edge, past the slip fielder for a brace.
Flatter and around middle. Temba Bavuma defends it to the leg side.
Tosses it up, outside off. Bavuma prods but keeps his bat away from the line of the ball.
This is darted on the pads. Keegan Petersen tucks it around the corner and settles for a single.
Floated, outside off. Keegan Petersen skips down the track and keeps it out.
Short of a length, outside off. Temba Bavuma cuts it nicely but fails to find the gap. He hits it straight to the backward point fielder. A wicket-maiden from Taskin Ahmed!
Pitches it up, outside off. Bavuma drives but Mehidy Hasan at extra cover dives to his left and stops it.
Around off. Temba Bavuma blocks it out.
Temba Bavuma is the new man in.

A loud shout for LBW but the umpire is unmoved! Bangladesh though have sent it upstairs. Was there any bat involved in it? No, says the UltraEdge! The Ball Tracker rolls in and it shows that the ball would have crashed into the middle stump. It is three reds. Lovely delivery from Taskin! This was a length ball, nipping back in just that little bit from off. Elgar sits back and tries to keep it out. He misses as the ball beats the inside edge of his bat. Elgar is pinged on the pads and Taskin Ahmed appeals. Bangladesh opt for a review as the on-field umpire doesn't agree. Three reds on the Ball Tracker and it is pumb in front. The on-field decision is overturned! Massive wicket for Bangladesh!
On a length and nipping back in from off. Dean Elgar prods and works it to mid on.
Play and a miss! Back of a length, well outside off. Elgar hangs back and throws his bat at it. The ball zips past his blade.
Floated, full and on off. Keegan Petersen comes down the track and drills it back to the bowler.
Keegan Petersen skips down the track and drives it to mid on.
Another ball, flatter and quicker, on a length, and spinning in from middle. Keegan Petersen works it towards mid-wicket.
Flatter ball, turning in from middle. Keegan Petersen rocks back and tucks it to square leg.
Full and on off. Keegan Petersen pushes it back to the bowler.
An appeal for LBW but the umpire says no! Tossed up, outside off. Keegan Petersen kneels and looks to reverse-sweep but he misses and gets hit on his pad. The impact might have been outside off.
An overpitched ball, outside off. Dean Elgar leans and pushes it to cover.
Good-length delivery, around off. Elgar gets behind the line of the ball and tucks it to mid-wicket.
A bit of inswing for Taskin! A length ball, jagging back in from outside off. Keegan Petersen looks to drive but it goes off the outer half towards deep cover for a run.
A full ball, outside off. Dean Elgar mistimes his drive towards cover and scampers through to the other end.
Short of a length, around off. Dean Elgar blocks it off the back foot.
On a length, outside off. Keegan Petersen taps it past the backward point fielder and takes a run.
A single to end the over! Full, on the pads. Keegan Petersen clips it to mid-wicket for a single.
On off, Keegan Petersen blocks it out watchfully.
Two runs now! Tossed up, around off. Keegan Petersen comes down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Elgar flicks a full delivery to mid-wicket for one.
Around off, pushed to cover.
Short, on off. Dean Elgar blocks it out.
Who will start from the other end? Mehidy Hasan it is.
It is length ball, outside off. Keegan Petersen shoulders his arms at it.
Full length, just outside off. Keegan Petersen blocks it out watchfully.
Outside off. Keegan Petersen leaves it alone for the keeper.
A length ball, on off. Keegan Petersen defends it out solidly.
FOUR! Keegan Petersen bags the first boundary post-Lunch session. Shorter in length, outside off. Keegan Petersen cuts it through covers for four.
Back of a length, outside off. Keegan Petersen lets it be.

We are back for the second session. The players of Bangladesh are in a huddle before they stride out to the middle. Dean Elgar and Keegan Petersen will resume their innings. Taskin Ahmed will start with the ball. Let's go..
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

For Bangladesh, it was Ebadot Hossain who set the tone for them as he started exceptionally well in the morning session. He got rid of Sarel Erwee but post that, nothing went their way. They were very sloppy in the slips and dropped a couple of catches. Dean Elgar took full advantage of that and went on to score another half-century. The pair of Keegan Petersen and Dean Elgar have stitched together an unbeaten stand of 57 runs and the Proteas would hope that they bat as deep as possible and set a massive target in front of Bangladesh. The tourists will need to make early inroads in the post-Lunch session if they are to win this Test match. Do join us for the middle session which begins at 4.25 pm IST (10.55 am GMT).

This has been a really good morning session for South Africa. They have managed to stretch their lead to 174, at the cost of just one wicket. Had Bangladesh held onto their catches, they could have found themselves in a much better position. The Proteas racked up 99 runs from 29 overs and they would be happier of the two sides going into the Lunch interval.
Short ball, outside off. Dean Elgar cuts it through cover for a brace. THAT WILL BE LUNCH AT DAY 4.
Tossed up, outside off. Dean Elgar drives it to cover.
Full, outside off. Dean Elgar pushes it out with his pad.
A single now as this is worked towards mid on.
Full toss, on off. Keegan Petersen comes down the track and hits it to the right of the bowler. Hasan dives to that side and makes a half-stop. The ball rolls to the man at mid on.
Fuller, outside off. Dean Elgar pushes it to cover for an easy single.
Length ball, on off, blocked out watchfully.
Halt in play. Keegan Petersen is getting his broken bat replaced.
Full length, on the off stump. Keegan Petersen drives it to mid on.
Full length, wide of off. Keegan Petersen steps forward and pushes it back to the bowler off the toe-end of the blade.
Ahmed bowls a length ball, angled into the pads. Keegan Petersen hangs back and flicks it to mid-wicket.
Fuller, outside off. Dean Elgar pushes it to cover for a quick single.
Full length, outside off. Dean Elgar leaves it alone for the keeper.
On off, blocked out watchfully.
Fuller, on off. It turns in off the deck. Keegan Petersen fails to flick it away. He gets pinged on his pads. Hasan appeals but the umpire shows no interest.
Tossed up, around off. Keegan Petersen blocks it to cover.
On off, defended out.
Flighted, full and outside off. It grips and turns in off the deck. Keegan Petersen shuffles across the stumps and takes a blow on his pads, outside the line though.
Fuller, on the pads. Dean Elgar clips it to square leg for a single. 100 is up for South Africa.
Fuller, on middle and leg. Keegan Petersen stays back, gets his blade down in time to block it out. Just a single of the over. Khaled Ahmed continues his good work with the ball.
Full length, on fifth stump. Keegan Petersen defends it to cover.
Back of a length, on the fourth stump line. Keegan Petersen pushes it to mid off.
Full, on off. Keegan Petersen pushes it gently towards mid off.
Length ball, on top of off. Keegan Petersen gets behind the line and blocks it out watchfully.
Back of a length, outside off. Dean Elgar cuts it to deep square leg for a single.

This is full and angled down leg. Keegan Petersen stays inside the crease. He tries to flick it away but misses. It might've brushed his pads. The fielders around the batter appeal for lbw, soon Hasan joins in with a stifled appeal. The umpire is unmoved. No review taken.
Fuller, on middle and leg. Keegan Petersen clips it past short leg.
Full, on the stumps. Keegan Petersen prods and defends it to the leg side.
Tossed up, around off. Dean Elgar pushes it to cover for one.
On off, Elgar eases it to mid on.
Loopy ball, around off, it turns down leg. Keegan Petersen flicks it to square leg with the turn for a single.
This one carries as well! A length ball, outside off. This one climbs off the deck. Dean Elgar shoulders his arms at it.
Back of a length, outside off. Dean Elgar shuffles across and shoulders his arms.

Swing and a miss! Good length, outside off, it flies off the deck. Dean Elgar stays back, tries to play away from his body. He gets beaten on the outside edge. Dean Elgar kicks the ground in frustration.
Fuller, on the pads. Keegan Petersen tries to flick it away to the leg side. The ball goes to cover off the leading edge. The batters cross for a single.
Full length, on the stumps. Keegan Petersen shuffles across and blocks it to mid-wicket off the inner half.
A length ball, on off. Keegan Petersen punches it through covers for a brace.
Fuller, on middle. Dean Elgar pats it back to the bowler.
Angled in on off. Dean Elgar blocks it on his front foot.
Full, on middle and leg. Keegan Petersen comes down the track, eases it to long on for a single.
On leg, defended to short mid on.

FOUR BYES! More extra runs. It is full and on leg. Keegan Petersen set himself up for the reverse-sweep but misses it completely. The ball goes past Mushfiqur Rahim at leg slip. It races away to the fine leg fence.
FOUR BYES! Misses everyone! It is looped up, around leg and turns away sharply. It goes past the keeper down to fine leg for a boundary. The umpire signals byes.
Length, on the pads. Keegan Petersen flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
On a length, defended out.
Length ball, on off, blocked out.

What a beautiful delivery. A length ball, outside off. It nips in off the deck. Keegan Petersen tries to defend it out but fails to do so on the front foot. Keegan Petersen gets hit on his thigh pad, in front of the stumps. Khaled Ahmed appeals but the umpire is unmoved and so is his skipper, Mominul Haque. Oh dear, the replays later show that the ball would have hit the stumps. Bangladesh camp is not happy. The umpires have not been on cue this morning.
Ahmed bangs in a short delivery, outside off. Keegan Petersen dabs it to point.
Back of a length, angling down the leg side. Keegan Petersen tries to flick it away but misses.
A bit short and outside off. Dean Elgar rocks back and pushes it to cover. Not in the gap though!
Nicely tossed up, outside off. Dean Elgar drives it to the mid off fielder.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Dean Elgar rocks back and cuts it to the cover fielder.
FOUR! Excellent timing on that one! An overpitched ball, around leg. Elgar prods and flicks it through the vacant square leg region for a boundary.
Floated, around middle. Keegan Petersen works it to square leg for a single.

A very loud shout for LBW but the umpire says no! This is a loopy ball, outside off and spinning in late. Keegan Petersen prods and looks to play it across the line. He misses and gets hit on his pad. The impact might have been outside off and hence, Bangladesh do not opt for a review.

FOUR! FIFTY FOR ELGAR! This was a bit uppish but well past the diving gully fielder. Back of a length, outside off. Elgar stays back and looks to push it through the off side. It goes off the outer half of the blade, past the gully fielder and races away to the fence. He raises his bat to the dressing room to take all the applause.
Full and around middle. Keegan Petersen flicks it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Short of a length, outside off. Dean Elgar pushes it through cover and collects a run. Elgar moves to 47!
A full ball, on middle. Keegan Petersen prods and pushes it to mid on. The batters cross ends.
On a length, around off. Keegan Petersen blocks it off the front foot.
Good-length ball, angling in from middle. Keegan Petersen stays back and tucks it to mid-wicket.
On a length, around off. Keegan Petersen defends it to the off side and collects a run.
FOUR! CRUNCHED! Short and wide, outside off. Keegan Petersen stands tall and cuts it uppishly past Mushfiqur Rahim at backward point for a boundary.
A length ball, way outside off. Keegan Petersen lets it be.
Good-length ball, outside off. Dean Elgar taps it to the off side and rotates the strike.

DROPPED! Oh, dear! Bangladesh have been really sloppy in the field this morning. Elgar gets a life! Back of a length, around the corridor of uncertainty. Elgar hangs hit bat around. It takes the thick outside edge towards Yasir Ali at second slip who puts it down. The ball goes past him and the batters take two runs. There is a direct hit at the striker's end but Elgar had made it home.
A length ball, nipping back in just that little bit from off. Dean Elgar blocks it off the back foot.
A bit quicker, around off. Keegan Petersen hangs back and dabs it onto the deck. The skipper starts with a maiden over!
On a length, outside off. Left alone.
Flatter and a bit quicker, around middle. Keegan Petersen rocks back and pushes it back to the bowler.
Looped up, on a length, outside off. Keegan Petersen prods and leaves it alone yet again.
Another ball, outside off. Keegan Petersen has no shot to offer.
Floated, full and outside off. Keegan Petersen leaves it alone.
Short of a length, outside off. Dean Elgar stays back and works it behind square on the off side for a couple of runs.
This is a length ball, outside off. Dean Elgar shoulders his arms to it.
Good-length ball, angling in from outside off. Dean Elgar covers his off pole and lets it be.
Nice and full, outside off. Dean Elgar leaves it alone.
On a length, around middle and leg. Keegan Petersen tucks it around the corner and rotates the strike.
Back of a length, just outside off. Keegan Petersen blocks it off the back foot.
A quicker ball, on a length, around middle. Dean Elgar stays back and nudges it behind square on the leg side for a couple of runs.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Keegan Petersen rocks back and cuts it to the cover fielder who half-stops it. A single taken!
Around off. Blocked out.
Darted on the pads. Elgar works it around the corner for a run.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Slightly shorter in length, outside off. Dean Elgar gets on top of the bounce and carves it through the cover region for a boundary.

DROPPED! Tossed up, well outside off. Dean Elgar reaches out and looks to drive it away from his body. It takes the outside edge and goes quickly towards Najmul Hossain Shanto, to his left, at first slip who spills it. A tough one but you expect that to be taken at this level.
FOUR! Top shot! A full ball, outside off. Keegan Petersen leans and drives it through the cover region for a boundary. He is off the mark in style!
On a length, around off. Keegan Petersen blocks it out.
Back of a length, around off and jagging back in sharply. Keegan Petersen stays back to defend but he gets an inside edge onto his pad.

DRINKS! A timely wicket for Bangladesh. Ebadot Hossain has been really impressive in the morning session. He was bending his back hard and eventually gets the reward for it. South Africa have ample wickets in hand to post a solid target on the board. Will Bangladesh be able to capitalize on this early breakthrough? Let us find out. Keegan Petersen walks out to bat at number 3 for South Africa.

An appeal for LBW but turned down! Bangladesh opt for a review! Three reds on the Ball Tracker and Erwee is a goner! Excellent review from Bangladesh, credit to the bowler as he was quite confident that he had got rid of Erwee and convinced his skipper as well. Ebadot Hossain finally gets his reward and he has been just brilliant in this morning session. This is a length ball, jagging back in late from outside off. Erwee prods and looks to play it across the line. He misses and gets pinged on his back pad. The Ball Tracker suggests that Erwee is plumb in front and the on-field decision is overturned.
Back of a length, around middle. Sarel Erwee tucks it to mid-wicket.
A short ball, outside off. Erwee cuts it to the point fielder.
Tossed up, outside off. Dean Elgar looks to sweep but he misses.
Hasan comes over the wicket now and serves a flatter ball, around leg. Elgar tickles it through fine leg for a couple of runs.
Tosses it up, well outside off. Dean Elgar leaves it alone watchfully.
This is a quicker ball, on a length, around middle. Elgar stays back and tucks it to square leg with soft hands.
Full and around middle. Elgar works it to mid-wicket.
Tossed up, around off. Elgar keeps it out.

Inside edge saves Erwee this time! Back of a length, nipping back in from outside off. Erwee looks to defend but he gets an inside edge onto his thigh pad. Hossain yet again exchanges some words with the batter. Excellent bowling from Ebadot! A maiden!
On a length and way outside off. Sarel Erwee lets it through to the keeper.
Fuller in length, outside off. Sarel Erwee lets it be.
Short of a length, outside off. Erwee shoulders his arms at it.
Around off. Blocked out.

A loud shout for LBW but the umpire shakes his head! Hossain comes 'round the wicket and hurls a full ball, angling in from middle. Erwee looks to flick it behind square on the leg side but he misses and gets hit on his pad. The replays suggest that the ball would have surely gone down leg.
This is an arm ball, around middle and going on with the angle. Dean Elgar tucks it wide of the mid-wicket fielder for a couple of runs.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Dean Elgar cuts it through the cover regio for a couple of runs.
Floated, on a length, outside off and spinning away late. Dean Elgar gets forward to defend but the ball zips past his outside edge.

An appeal for LBW but the umpire is unmoved! Hasan goes wide of the crease and serves a quicker ball, on a length, just outside off. Dean Elgar prods and pads it away. Bangladesh do not opt for a review.
Flatter ball, on a length, outside off. Dean Elgar prods and leaves it alone.
A low full toss, around leg. Elgar flicks it through the square leg region for a brace. A rare loose delivery from Mehidy Hasan!
A single to end the over! Length ball, outside off. Dean Elgar works it to point for a single.
Length ball, outside off. Dean Elgar defends it to mid off.
Length, on the pads. Sarel Erwee clips it to square leg for a single.
Full length, outside off. Dean Elgar defends it to cover on the front foot for a single.
Length, on off, defended out.
Full length, angled in on off. Dean Elgar walks forward and blocks it back to the bowler.
LEG BYE! Angled down the leg side. Elgar fails to pick it up. The ball brushes the pads and rolls towards fine leg. The batters take a leg bye.
On middle and leg, tucked to short leg.
Floated, full and outside off. It stays low a tad as it turns away. Dean Elgar cuts it to cover.
Looped up, on off. Dean Elgar stays back and blocks it out watchfully.
Full, on off. Dean Elgar defends it to point.
Fuller, on the fourth stump. Sarel Erwee drives it to covers for an easy single.
LEG BYE! Length ball, on the pads, Sarel Erwee fails to flick it away. He gets pinged on his pads. Ebadot Hossain makes a stifled appeal but the umpire shows no interest. They cross for a leg bye.
A length ball, on the pads. Elgar clips it to square leg for a single.

Full length, on off. Dean Elgar blocks it back to the bowler. Ebadot Hossain throws the ball down the leg side. Liton Das, behind the sticks, had to work extremely hard to stop the ball. Ebadot Hossain is clearly frustrated and he has a chat with Elgar before the umpire intervenes.
Touch short, on off. Dean Elgar hops and clips it to mid-wicket. Dean Elgar ventures out looking for a single, but Sarel Erwee does well to deny it.

FOUR! Dean Elgar bags another boundary in the morning session. Too straight, on the pads. Dean Elgar flicks it to fine leg for a boundary. The lead is into the three figures now. It is 102 to be precise.
Back of a length, outside off. Dean Elgar shoulders his arms at it.
Ebadot Hossain comes into the attack.
Fuller, on the pads. Sarel Erwee clips it to mid-wicket.
Tossed up, full and outside off. Elgar taps it to point for a quick single.
Fuller, outside off, turning away. Elgar lets it be.
On the pads, Sarel Erwee flicks it to square leg for a single.
Short, outside off. Sarel Erwee cuts it to cover.
Floated, full and around off. Sarel Erwee leans in and tries to defend it out but misses. The ball zips past the outside edge.
FOUR! Top shot! Much better from Elgar. Full length, angled into the pads. Dean Elgar waits for it and places it to perfection past mid on for a boundary.
Length ball, on off. Elgar defends it out watchfully.
EDGED BUT SHORT! A full-length ball, on off. Dean Elgar tries to work it to the leg side. The ball takes the outside edge and lands short of the man at first slip.
Length ball, on off. Blocked out.
Full length, on the pads, Elgar tucks it to short mid-wicket.
Back of a length, outside off. Elgar taps it to backward point.
Floated, on a length, around off. Erwee defends it off the front foot. A maiden over from Hasan!
Play and a miss! Hasan serves a loopy ball, well outside off. Sarel Erwee reaches out and looks to slap it through the cover region. The ball goes past his outside edge.
An arm ball, going on with the angle, outside off. Sarel Erwee stays back and punches it to the cover fielder.
Flatter and quicker, around off. Sarel Erwee blocks it out watchfully.
Full and around off. Sarel Erwee defends it off the front foot.
Tossed up, on off. Sarel Erwee keeps it out.
FOUR! SMASHED! Good-length delivery, around off. Dean Elgar hangs back and caresses it through the cover region for a boundary.
Back of a length, around middle. Dean Elgar dabs it onto the deck.
Full and outside off. Dean Elgar sits back and lets it be.
Chopped on, almost! On a length and shaping away from off. Dean Elgar looks to push it through cover but it goes off the thick inside edge just past the leg stump.
Short of a length, well outside off. Dean Elgar lets it sail through to the keeper.
Back of a length, outside off. Dean Elgar does not bother playing at it.
Full and around off. Sarel Erwee pushes it back to the bowler. A maiden over!
A quicker ball, full and outside off. Sarel Erwee lets it be.
Tossed up delivery, outside off. Sarel Erwee leaves it alone.
Floated, full and outside off. Sarel Erwee stretches forward and defends.
Flatter and quicker, around off. Sarel Erwee covers the line and dabs it onto the deck.
Nicely tossed up, around off. Sarel Erwee keeps it out.
Fuller and wider, outside off. Dean Elgar shoulders his arms at it.
Shorter in length, angling across the batter, from just outside off. Dean Elgar lets it through to the keeper.
Back of a length, outside off. Dean Elgar hangs back and pushes it to cover.
Fuller in length, around off. Dean Elgar pushes it back past the bowler for a couple of runs.
BEATEN! A length ball, just outside off and shaping away from the batter. Dean Elgar feels for it but the ball rips past his outside edge.
Good-length ball, angling across the batter from outside off. Dean Elgar lets it be.
Tosses it up, around off. Sarel Erwee keeps it out.
Shorter in length, outside off. Dean Elgar cuts it through covers for a run.
On a length, around off. Dean Elgar keeps it out.

An appeal for LBW but the umpire is not interested! Bangladesh have opted for a review. Umpire's call on wickets hitting and Dean Elgar survives! Tossed up, on middle and turning away late. Elgar prods to defend but the ball spins past his blade and hits his back pad. The UltraEdge rolls in and it shows that the ball would have clipped the off stump. Bangladesh do not lose their review this time. Also, it is four byes as the ball rolls away to the third man fence.
FOUR! This is sliding down leg. Dean Elgar gets forward and just tickles it through the fine leg region for a boundary.
Nicely tossed up, around off. Dean Elgar prods and keeps it out.
On a length, around leg. Erwee tucks it around the corner for a brace.
A length ball, angling across the batter. Sarel Erwee does not bother playing at it.
Full and outside off. Erwee leaves it alone.
On a length, and way outside off. Left alone.
Good-length delivery, around off. He blocks it off the front foot.
On a length, and outside off. Sarel Erwee leaves it alone.

The morning session is set to begin. The Bangladesh players stride out to the middle. Followed by Dean Elgar and Sarel Erwee who walk to bat for South Africa. Just a short update as well, all the session have been extended by 15 mins due to early stumps on Day 3. Khaled Ahmed to start the proceedings with the ball.

Lizaad Williams is in for a chat. He says it still feels unreal to bag three wickets. Mentions all the nerves are gone now. Says he will try to make the most of it in the second innings. Says he is just happy that he could contribute for the team. Adds, he believes his strength is hitting the wicket hard and he focused on doing that. Hopes to be more consistent in the second innings. Says, there is no hassle with his skin condition.

Rangana Herath, the bowling consultant of Bangladesh is up for a chat. He says that there will be some assistance for the spinners and the role of Mehidy Hasan would be very crucial going into Day 4. Adds that there is a lot of potential in this Bangladesh side and they need to be given confidence. Tells that Najmul Hossain Shanto is also a good bowler but he needs to be a bit more confident about his skills. Mentions that the pace bowlers will need to play the supporting role for Mehidy Hasan going ahead in this Test. Says that South Africa is ahead at the moment but he believes that Bangladesh will play their best cricket on the last two days.

Bangladesh, on the other hand, showed grit and determination with the blade on Day 3, but could not cut down the deficit. Bangladesh bowlers have their task cut out now. Taking wickets in each session would be the key for the visitors if they are to restrict South Africa to an average score. Let us hope we get full day’s play. Who will dominate the morning session? Stay tuned to find out.

Hello and a warm welcome to all! It is time for Day 4 of the first Test match between South Africa and Bangladesh. Even though the entertainment was cut short due to bad light, the officials were forced to call it Stumps on Day 3, as the rain gods had the last say. South Africa still have all their wickets in hand and would hope to post a mammoth total on the board.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

South Africa though would have loved to end things pretty earlier but their bowlers were made to toil hard. In the end, they did manage to end Bangladesh’s innings with a lead of 69 runs. Although, the start of the third innings was not a good one, as bad light forced Bangladesh to bowl two spinners after the opening over of Khaled Ahmed. Even this did not go as per plan, as the rain gods had the final say on the moving day. Will the conditions favour South Africa to bat on Day 4? To find out, do join us on Sunday at 1330 IST (0800 GMT). But you can join us early for the build-up. Till then, take care and goodbye.

Bangladesh came to bat on Day 3 in a precarious position, it could have gotten worse for them if not for Joy’s knock. He was the sole back bone of their innings. Joy was the first one to get on the crease for the visitors and the last one to show his back to South Africa. The 21-year-old made history by becoming the first Bangladeshi batter to score a ton against South Africa in Tests.

What a day of Test cricket it was! Although, not the end that we were hoping for. South Africa end Day 3 with a lead of 75 runs. They would look to bat for at least two complete sessions on Day 4 and hope to set up a huge target on the board. Bangladesh would be gutted by their overall batting performance, but there is a new star born for them in Mahmudul Hasan Joy.

UPDATE 1941 IST (1411 GMT) - OH NO! The inevitable has happened. The play has been stopped due to bad light. To make it even worse, the rain gods have spoken as well, with a slight drizzle. The ground staff hurries onto the field to cover the pitch. Looks like the chances are really slim for the action to resume. Let us see what the officials decide. Stay tuned for further updates.

Ouch! That might have hurt! An overthrow and they get the single in the end. This was tossed up, around off. Sarel Erwee pushes it to cover. The fielder there, collects the ball and has a shy at the striker's end. However, the ball hits Yasir Ali at silly point who tries to duck under it. Ali gets hit on his helmet and the ball ricochets past the keeper. The batters steal a single.
On a length, around off. Sarel Erwee dead-bats it.
Slightly shorter in length, outside off. Dean Elgar cuts it to the backward point fielder. The fielder there half-stops it and the batters take a single.
On a length, outside off. Dean Elgar leans but lets the ball go through to the keeper.
Floated, around off. Dean Elgar prods to keep it out.
Flatter and quicker, around off. Dean Elgar rocks back to defend it.
BEATEN! Floated, full and outside off. Sarel Erwee looks to defend but the ball spins past his outside edge.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Dean Elgar works it through the off side and collects a single.
Shorter in length, outside off. Sarel Erwee punches it through cover and rotates the strike.
On a length, outside off. Sarel Erwee pushes it to cover.
Around middle. Dean Elgar tucks it to the leg side for a run.

An appeal for caught behind but the umpire is not interested! Bangladesh have opted for a review though! This is tossed up, well outside off. Dean Elgar reaches out and looks to drive but the ball spins past his outside edge. The keeper collects the ball and they appeal. The umpire says no and Bangladesh take it upstairs. The UltraEdge rolls in and it shows that there was no deflection when the ball passed the bat. The on-field decision stands.

Change. With the bad light being as issue. Najmul Hossain Shanto gets the ball in hand to work his spin from the other end. He replaces Khaled Ahmed. This shows how much both these sides want to keep playing.
Turn and bounce! Floated, full and outside off. Sarel Erwee looks to drive away from his body. He misses as the ball rips past his outside edge. Mehidy Hasan starts with a maiden over!
An arm ball that goes on with the angle, from off. Sarel Erwee keeps it out.
Floated, full and outside off. Erwee prods and defends it to point.
A quicker ball, going on with the arm from middle. Sarel Erwee stays back and tucks it to mid-wicket.
Flatter and outside off. Sarel Erwee rocks back and punches it to the cover fielder.
Nicely tossed up, around off. Sarel Erwee pushes it back to the bowler.

Who will bowl from the other end? It will be Mehidy Hasan to work his spin from the other end. Although, the umpire are keeping the light-o-meter handy. It is getting dark around the venue, but the artifical lights are helping to keep the game on at the moment. Maybe, that is why Mominul Haque went with a spinner straightaway.
A length ball, nipping back in from well outside off. Elgar lets it be.
Back of a length, around leg. Sarel Erwee tucks it around the corner and takes a run. Erwee and South Africa are up and running!
A length ball, jagging away from outside off. Sarel Erwee dabs it onto the deck.
Back of a length, around off. Sarel Erwee hangs back to defend this one.
On a length, around off. Sarel Erwee keeps it out.
BEAUTY! Good-length delivery, around off and shaping away late. Erwee pokes at it but the ball zips past his outside edge.
